title: Keysight ADS Enables First-Pass Silicon at 3 THz for AttoTude - Semiwiki
gist: AttoTude used Keysight's Advanced Design System to build an IC flow spanning 100 GHz to 3 THz, cutting development cycles by more than 50% and reaching concept-to-tape-out in under six weeks with repeated first-pass silicon success. The company is commercializing a wired THz interconnect (AttoEngine ASIC plus AttoWire dielectric waveguide) targeting 200/400/800 Gbit/s per lane for AI and hyperscale data centers, aiming at optical-class bandwidth density without lasers or modulators.

insights.claim: AttoTude reports that expanding its use of Keysight Advanced Design System across a 100-GHz-to-3-THz IC flow cut IC development cycles by more than 50%, moving projects from concept to tape-out in under six weeks.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: A concrete, quantified EDA productivity claim in the hardest RF regime — supportive of Keysight's high-frequency design software franchise and its pricing power in RF/mmWave EDA.
insights.quote: reduced IC development cycles by more than 50%, enabling projects to move from concept to tape-out in less than six weeks
insights.locator: AttoTude has expanded its use of Keysight

insights.claim: First-pass silicon is economically decisive at terahertz frequencies because a respin adds fabrication expense and can delay system evaluation by months, while post-fabrication tuning options are limited — making predictive simulation fidelity central to development economics.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Explains why EDA spend per design scales superlinearly at the frontier: simulation accuracy substitutes directly for respin cost, sustaining premium tool pricing.
insights.quote: At THz frequencies, post-fabrication tuning options are limited, making predictive simulation fidelity central to development economics.
insights.locator: The reported first-pass results are technically significant

insights.claim: AttoTude ASIC architect Richard Chan attributes the team's ability to work faster and repeatedly reach functional silicon on the first attempt to the accuracy of Keysight's EDA software.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: A named customer reference for Keysight EDA in an emerging AI-infrastructure category — the kind of proof point that converts into design-win momentum.
insights.locator: According to AttoTude ASIC architect Richard Chan

themes.theme: THz interconnect as an optics alternative

insights.claim: AttoTude is building a wired THz interconnect platform for AI and hyperscale data centers that pairs an ASIC-based signal generator (AttoEngine) with low-loss dielectric waveguides (AttoWire) to deliver optical-class bandwidth density while avoiding lasers, optical modulators and other power-intensive photonic components.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: A credible third architecture between copper and optics in the scale-up interconnect fight — a potential competitive threat to optical-module and co-packaged-optics suppliers if it reaches volume.
insights.quote: The objective is to provide the bandwidth density associated with optical links while avoiding lasers, optical modulators and other power-intensive photonic components.
insights.locator: AttoTude is developing a wired THz interconnect platform

insights.claim: AttoTude is targeting per-lane data rates of 200, 400 and 800 Gbit/s, explicitly aimed at scale-up connectivity for increasingly large AI accelerator clusters.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: These per-lane targets are directly comparable to next-generation optical and SerDes roadmaps — a benchmark for judging whether THz-over-dielectric is competitive or merely novel.
insights.locator: Target per-lane data rates include 200, 400 and 800 Gbit/s

insights.claim: AI systems are pushing electrical channels toward severe limits in reach, bandwidth and energy efficiency while photonics carries its own cost and integration challenges, leaving open a distinct design space of electromagnetic transmission at very high carrier frequencies implemented in scalable semiconductor technology.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Frames the interconnect bottleneck as a three-way contest rather than copper-versus-optics — worth watching for hyperscaler evaluation programs that could reprice optical suppliers.
insights.quote: AttoTude’s transistor-driven THz-over-dielectric approach occupies a different design space
insights.locator: The collaboration also illustrates a broader change

insights.claim: Reaching first-pass silicon across designs extending to 3 THz suggests THz IC development is moving from laboratory experimentation toward a repeatable engineering discipline and potentially toward deployable, high-volume interconnect products for AI infrastructure.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Repeatability is the gating condition for THz interconnect to become an investable category rather than a research curiosity; treat this as an early-stage watch item.

themes.theme: Why THz breaks conventional IC methodology

insights.claim: Above 100 GHz an on-chip conductor stops behaving as a simple lumped connection: interconnect length, geometry, substrate coupling, return-current paths and metal-stack properties produce distributed electromagnetic effects that conventional digital IC methodologies cannot resolve.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Explains why THz design requires a fundamentally different EDA toolchain — a structural moat for RF/EM-native vendors like Keysight versus digital-flow incumbents.
insights.quote: At these frequencies, an on-chip conductor is no longer a simple lumped connection.

insights.claim: Parasitic inductance and capacitance, conductor and dielectric loss, dispersion, skin effect, impedance discontinuities and unintended radiation can materially change circuit behavior at THz frequencies, so schematic-level transistor simulations must be correlated with electromagnetic models of the physical layout.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Identifies EM-circuit co-simulation as the non-optional capability in this segment — a purchasing requirement that narrows the vendor field.

insights.claim: A circuit that looks stable and well matched in an ideal simulation can shift in frequency or lose gain after extraction, because small geometric changes alter phase, impedance and coupling and errors that are negligible at microwave frequencies become significant fractions of a wavelength in the THz regime.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Quantifies the error-amplification mechanism that makes THz respins likely without integrated EM flows — the technical basis for the tool-spend argument.
insights.quote: model or layout errors that seem negligible at microwave frequencies become significant fractions of a wavelength in the THz regime
insights.locator: A design that appears stable and properly matched

insights.claim: Keysight ADS provides one environment for circuit design, layout, electromagnetic analysis and system-level verification, letting a team model active devices together with extracted passive structures and compare architectural alternatives before committing a mask set — reducing translation errors and model inconsistencies that arise when data moves manually between point tools.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Integration, not any single engine, is the sales argument — supports platform bundling economics over per-tool competition in RF EDA.
insights.locator: Keysight ADS provides a common environment

insights.claim: System-level scenario planning — assessing link budgets, modulation requirements, channel characteristics and implementation trade-offs before transistor-level optimization is complete — lets system constraints flow into the IC design and reduces the risk of a circuit that meets an isolated block specification but fails in the full interconnect.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Top-down system-to-circuit methodology is where EDA vendors are extending scope; a growth vector beyond seat-count expansion.
insights.locator: System-level scenario planning is another important element

insights.claim: AttoTude uses Keysight design-data-management software for revision control so it can identify which model and layout revisions produced a result, reproduce earlier simulations and coordinate concurrent changes across electromagnetic models, schematics, layouts, PDK elements and verification results.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Design-data management is a sticky, recurring-revenue attach to simulation tools — evidence of Keysight monetizing the Cliosoft-style data layer alongside ADS.
insights.locator: AttoTude also uses Keysight design-data-management software
